reason: Reproduced in ~/Coding/ge-wt/rev-proto/src/tensor/review_proto_test.zig. Tests 'R3a ext key with a SUM label must not bound each entry of a matmul operand' and 'R3b ext key on a FIX0 slice ...' fail (run: cd src/tensor && memguard run --gb 6 -- zig build test -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe). Output: "R3(SUM): verifier ACCEPTED; X = { 1073741824, 1073741824, 0, 0, -1073741821, -1073741821, 5, 5 }, integer acc[0]=2147483648 ... proved Y = { 1, 1, 1, 1, 3, 3, 3, 3 }" and "R3(FIX0): verifier ACCEPTED; ... acc[4]=2147483648, proved Y = { 3, 3, 3, 3, 1, 1, 1, 1 }". In protocol.zig:1255-1265 the key branch checks only terms.len==1, coeff ±1 and !public. It never looks at the labels or at k.n, then calls setb on the whole tensor. Line 1277 accepts the operand and line 1278 passes the 8+7+2 ≤ 30 check, so the result is a mod-p wrap that the verifier accepts. I tried to refute it: the statement is public, so a cheating prover cannot pick it alone. No shipped builder emits a slice-only or SUM-only key on a base matmul or hadamard operand (transformer.zig uses SUM/FIX labels only in lineq and einsum, and sliceFix on Q/K/V einsum labels). But the validateStatement doc comment (protocol.zig:1203-1210) names this check as the soundness gate, and verify() relies on it. Any statement that passes it is supposed to have integer semantics. It stays high because the bug is a silent inference error, not a documented delegation. It could drop to medium if statements are always trusted builder output.
fix: In the .key branch at protocol.zig:1255, derive a bound only when the term's labels are exactly n distinct variable ids (no SUM, no FIX0/FIX1, each in [0,k.n) and none repeated) and k.n == st.witness[id].logSize(), so every entry is checked exactly once. Otherwise leave bound at 255. If slice keys must bound operands, track a covered-bitmask per tensor and set the bound only when the union of the slices covers every index.

reason: Reproduced. Test 'R2 exact ext einsum output as matmul operand: unbounded X must be rejected' fails with "R2: verifier ACCEPTED Y=1 for X.W = 2^31 (X entries 2^30, no range relation); validateStatement passed". protocol.zig:1248-1253 assigns EXT_EXACT_BOUND to any exact einsum output whose operands are free witnesses. Lines 1277-1278 and 1283-1284 then skip both the unbounded check and the accumulator check. The relaxation is deliberate and documented as 'the ext builder's responsibility' (transformer.zig:829 feeds an exact MoE dispatch output xe into b.matmul at :831). The honest path is sound only because LayerCfg.validate runs on the prover side, and verify() never runs it. So a statement that is not from a builder gets accepted with wrapped arithmetic. It is medium, not high, because the delegation is documented and the honest builder is correct. I did not exercise the claim that honest prove() overflows the i32 in matmulAcc; it is plausible only.
fix: Replace the EXT_EXACT_BOUND marker with a real propagated bound. For an exact einsum, bound(y) = bound(a) + bound(b) + n_k, where a public operand contributes ceil(log2(max|values|)) and a weight contributes 7. Evaluate the ext and base ops in dependency order (or iterate to a fixpoint), and return StatementUnboundedOperand when an operand's bound is unknown. Then apply the ordinary 2^30 accumulator checks to every operand, with no EXT_EXACT_BOUND exemption. For MoE dispatch, a proved one-hot selector (a 0/1 range key on sel/disp) gives bound(disp)=0, so bound(xe)=7+0+0, which keeps the honest path valid.

reason: Reproduced. 'R1 batch_matmuls: two same-shape matmuls (class is last) verify' fails with "R1: honest proof rejected with batch_matmuls=true: ProofShape", and the same statement verifies with batch_matmuls=false. At protocol.zig:1453, `if (op_i >= proof.op_sumchecks.len) return error.ProofShape;` runs before the `if (vclass_done[i]) continue;` at 1455. When the last remainder keys are non-first members of an already-verified class, op_i equals len and the honest proof is rejected. This is a completeness bug that affects any statement ending in a batched class (stacked same-shape layers, gate/up or QKV classes at the end).
fix: Move the skip above the shape check: `if (cfg.batch_matmuls and st.ops[k.op] == .matmul and vclass_done[i]) continue;` and only then `if (op_i >= proof.op_sumchecks.len) return error.ProofShape;`. Also add a final `if (op_i != proof.op_sumchecks.len) return error.ProofShape;` after the loop (if one is not already present) so that extra trailing sumchecks are rejected.

reason: Reproduced with REVIEW_PANIC=1 and the opt-in test 'R5 validateStatement with ext einsum y out of range'. Output: "panic: index out of bounds: index 9, len 2 ... protocol.zig:1246:29 in validateStatement". verify() calls validateStatement (1304) before xt.validate (1305). Lines 1246 and 1252 read and write bound[y] with no y < n guard; setb has a guard, but those raw accesses do not. Line 1260 indexes st.ext.tables[id] unchecked. TensorInfo.logSize (protocol.zig:54) slices log_dims[0..n_dims] without checking n_dims. In ReleaseFast the 1252 write is an out-of-bounds stack write of the byte 254, beyond bound_buf when y ≥ 4096. That is memory corruption from statement input, so I raise it from low to medium. It stays low if statements are always trusted.
fix: In verify(), run xt.validate(st) plus a core shape pass before the bound pass. The shape pass checks every tensor id < n, table ids < tables.len, and n_dims ≤ MAX_DIMS for witness and weights, and caps log sizes. Inside validateStatement, replace the raw bound[y] accesses with guarded ones (`if (y >= n) return error.StatementShape;`) and check `id < st.ext.tables.len` before indexing at 1260.

reason: Code inspection agrees: at protocol.zig:1478 only st.weights[m.w].log_dims are checked, while the point comes from key.offsets[m.w] and key.infos[m.w].logSize(). Nothing enforces key.infos.len == st.weights.len or that the shapes are equal. key.root is mixed into the transcript but infos and offsets are not. A cheating prover cannot exploit this: WeightKey is verifier-held data built by weightKey(&ws). So the risk is a crash (out-of-bounds index or a memcpy length mismatch in fullPoint) or a silent reshape when the key and the statement come from different sources. I did not write a test.
fix: At the start of verify(): require key.infos.len == st.weights.len, key.offsets.len == key.infos.len, and std.meta.eql(key.infos[i], st.weights[i]) for every i. Return error.StatementShape otherwise. Also mix the key's infos and offsets into the transcript, or derive them from st.weights alone.

reason: This is the standard LogUp field-characteristic requirement. Per-table key multiplicities are M31 elements, so p = 2^31-1 copies of an off-table key value contribute p/(α-v) = 0. validateStatement caps the tensor count (4096) but not log sizes (no cap besides MAXB for publics and tables, per ext.zig:200-203). So a statement with ≥ p total key entries on one table is allowed. Exploiting this needs a witness of more than 2^31 entries, so I did not demonstrate it.
fix: In validateStatement, accumulate Σ 2^log_size over all key instances (base range8/lookup/glu and ext keys) per table, and reject when the sum is ≥ 2^30. Also cap each witness tensor's logSize (for example at ≤ 30) so that the sum cannot overflow.

reason: I re-ran the suite in ~/Coding/ge-wt/rev-pcs/src/tensor with `memguard run --gb 6 --label review-pcs-skeptic -- zig build test -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe --summary all`. Result: 66/66 passed, with these prints: '[review hybrid] t=4 rho=1/4: M2 (false) opening accepted 34/512; key(M1)+batch(M2) both accepted 5/512; conjectured per-opening bound rho^t*n = 2.0' and '[review e2e hybrid] t=2: key(M1)+batch(M2) accepted after 8 hybrid seeds'. Both tests assert that the attack is accepted. I tried to refute it and could not. (1) protocol.zig:1565-1573 opens the weights per batch with with_proximity=false, in both the flat path and the pcs2 path. (2) Neither the witness commitment nor anything else in the batch transcript ties the decoding to the one the key proof saw. The key transcript (weight_key.zig:64-68) and the batch transcript are independent, so the key proof and each batch proof can be ground separately. (3) In the e2e test M2 is a valid int8 model (down projection negated), so the result is a real model swap, not only an out-of-range trick. 34/512 matches (1/2)^t; rho^t would predict 2/512. The acceptance rate is about (1-delta)^t for a word at distance delta from both codewords. That is exactly the unique-decoding rate provenBits already uses (pcs.zig:43-49). At t=54, lb=2, pow=20 that is 2^-56.6, which equals provenBits(). So the 'conjectured 128-bit' figure in conjecturedBits (pcs.zig:39-41, pcs2.zig:75-77) has no backing for openings without OOD/proximity. The capacity-style conjecture covers proximity only, not binding to a unique codeword. FlashProve gets that binding from OOD samples (paper.txt:75-78) plus link proofs for copies. Not demonstrated: the ((1+rho)/2)^t vanishing-difference variant. It needs M2-M1 whose row encodings vanish on about C-1 points, which generally forces M2 out of int8. The verifier would then lose the int8 accumulator bound in validateStatement. This variant is PLAUSIBLE, but it does not change the verdict. The half-split attack alone gives about 2^74 work per forged batch at the advertised parameters, far below 128.
fix: (a) Immediately: stop presenting conjecturedBits as the security level of any configuration whose weight opening runs without proximity. Report provenBits for those configurations. For 128 bits at lb=2, pow=20 this needs t ≥ ceil(108/-log2(5/8)) = 160. Rewrite pcs.zig:16-19 ('decoded rows are already fixed' holds only within unique decoding, delta < (1-rho)/2, and only with a proven proximity bound) and the README/size.md claims. Re-run the size comparison (size.md §5) with those query counts. (b) Proper fix, as in FlashProve and WHIR: in weight_key.prove, after the root is fixed, derive z_ood ∈ QM31^(log_rows+log_cols) from the key transcript and publish v_ood = W(z_ood) in KeyProof. Include that claim in the key proof's proximity opening group. Store (z_ood, v_ood) in WeightKey. In every batch verify, add the claim (z_ood, v_ood) to the weight opening groups (for pcs2, to the groupByColumn output). Then a batch decoding that differs from the key's decoding must also match the published OOD value, which fails except with probability about L·deg/|F| per list element (Johnson/list-size analysis). With OOD in place, the per-batch opening also needs proximity so that the list-decoding regime applies: call it with with_proximity=true, or add an explicit link proof as FlashProve does. Otherwise per-batch soundness still falls back to unique decoding.

reason: Test 'review: weight key proof does not bind tensor offsets - swapped layout accepted' (review_pcs_test.zig:263) passes. With the root unchanged and the offsets of gate and up swapped, wk.verify(key2, honest key proof) and proto.verify(swapped-model proof, key2) both pass, and the outputs differ. Code confirms it: startTranscript (weight_key.zig:64-68) mixes only the root, log_rows, log_cols and rows_used, and mixStatement (protocol.zig:493-517) mixes only key.root. verify (protocol.zig:1304+) never checks key.infos or key.offsets against st.weights, and fullPoint (protocol.zig:521-531) trusts key.offsets[m.w] and key.infos[m.w]. Mitigating factor: the WeightKey is a verifier input, so this is a soundness break only if the layout comes from the prover or server instead of from a trusted configuration. FlashProve fixes the layout with a public layout file and a parameter check (paper.txt:655-658). That is why I rate it medium, not high. The panic paths I confirmed by reading the code only; I did not execute them, since a panic would kill the runner. key.offsets/key.infos shorter than st.weights gives an index out-of-bounds panic. key.infos[m.w].logSize() > log_total gives a u32 underflow at `nb = log_total - log_size` (:523). A logSize that disagrees with the statement-derived pw length gives a @memcpy length-mismatch panic (:529). A misaligned offset is silently truncated by `offset >> log_size` (:524). All of these are ReleaseSafe panics, or silent misbehaviour, on verifier inputs instead of errors.
fix: In proto.verify, before the transcript, validate the key against the statement and return errors, not panics. Require key.infos.len == key.offsets.len == st.weights.len, and require each key.infos[i] to equal st.weights[i] (dims). Recompute `layout(st.weights)` and require identical offsets (which implies alignment), key.log_rows + key.log_cols == lay.log_total, and rows_used == ceil(lay.used / 2^log_cols). Add a defensive check in fullPoint as well: log_size <= log_total, local.len == log_size, offset % 2^log_size == 0. Then mix the full layout (n tensors, each info's dims, each offset) into both weight_key.startTranscript and mixStatement, so that the key proof and every batch proof commit to one layout.

reason: Test 'review: flat weight opening with weight_log_cols > min log N rejects an honest proof' (review_pcs_test.zig:477) prints '[review wlc] verify result: error.OpeningGroupMismatch' and passes. An honest prover with two_level=null and weight_log_cols=5 > log_d=4 produces a proof that its own verifier rejects. commitWeights (protocol.zig:187-203) only clamps lc to log_total. The 'must be <= min log N' comment (protocol.zig:166-167) is not enforced, and the default weight_log_cols=10 breaks any flat-PCS model with a matmul of N < 2^10. This is a completeness failure only: it never leads to wrong acceptance.
fix: Use pcs2.groupByColumn(wcl, key.log_rows) in the flat branch too (protocol.zig:1572-1576). The prover side must group the same way. Alternatively, reject the configuration at commitWeights, prove and verify with an explicit error (e.g. error.WeightLogColsTooLarge) when weight_log_cols > min over matmuls of log N, or clamp it.

reason: Confirmed in the code: verifyOpening calls groupCoeffs at pcs.zig:535, which slices c.point[0..log_rows] (pcs.zig:436), before the point-length check at pcs.zig:543. A short point causes an out-of-bounds slice panic in ReleaseSafe. It is not reachable today. Every point reaching pcs.verifyOpening is built by the verifier: fullPoint returns length key.log_rows + key.log_cols = kshape's sum, and the witness point is bv.point of length lay.log_total = split.lr + split.lc. Only protocol.zig:1587 and the in-file tests call it. So this is hardening only.
fix: In pcs.verifyOpening, before drawGammas or groupCoeffs, loop over all groups and claims and return error.OpeningShape if c.point.len != shape.log_rows + shape.log_cols. This matches the ordering in pcs2.verifyRec.

reason: I re-ran ~/Coding/ge-wt/rev-ext/src/tensor/review_ext_test.zig 'review: softmax reciprocal wraps mod p at lt = 8 (cheating rden accepted)' under memguard --gb 6 with ReleaseSafe. Output: 'lt=8 den=65536 rden honest=128 cheat=32895; P[T-1,0] honest=1 cheat=128; O[T-1] honest=1 cheat=64; sum_j P cheat=32768' and then 'VERIFIER ACCEPTED the cheating softmax reciprocal'. I tried to refute it three ways and could not. (1) xt.test_unchecked_prover is used only at ext.zig:591/598/666/674, which are prover-side witness self-checks; the verifier path is unchanged. (2) At lt=8 every rangeWide is 16 bits, so it is a direct key (transformer.zig:235). There are no stale lo/hi limbs, so the edited witness is fully consistent. At lt>8 the limb decomposition is equivalent, so the attack carries over. (3) The arithmetic holds. rden'=floor((2^23+p)/2^16)=32895<2^16. pr'=rden'·den−p=8323073, so 2^K−pr'=65535, which passes both keys at 705-706. The P accumulator is e·rden' ≤ 2^(lt+16) < p and P stays within the 9-bit signed range. The attack works when den > 128+2^(23−lt), which is reachable at the bench configs lt=9 and lt=10 (scripts/tensor_compare.py:90) and up to lt=12 (validate at transformer.zig:406). The defect is at transformer.zig:703-706. The design-doc argument at transformer.md:209-210 and the table row at 233 bounds 2^K−pr but never the integer rden·den, which reaches 2^(2lt+16). Control check: the RMSNorm reciprocal at transformer.zig:579-588 uses the same pattern but is safe, since rt<2^12 and inv<2^16 give a product below 2^28.
fix: Make every exact product provably below p. Preferred fix: remove rden and prove the softmax-weighted output the FlashProve way. Compute acc[t,h,c]=Σ_j e·v as an exact einsum (|acc| ≤ 2^(lt+15)). Then prove o=round(acc/den) with a per-entry division inequality 0 ≤ 2·acc+den−2·o·den < 2·den, where o is range-checked so that |o·den| < 2^30. A minimal patch instead keeps P but proves P directly: 0 ≤ 256e+den−2P·den < 2den with P ∈ [0,2^9), so P·den ≤ 2^(lt+17) < p. Until either lands, LayerCfg.validate should reject log_t ≥ 8. Also correct transformer.md §3 and the §4 row 'pr = rden den'.

reason: I reproduced it with 'review: validateStatement infers a full-tensor bound from a FIX-slice / SUM range key'. With no key the result is StatementUnboundedOperand. With a key on X[FIX0,c] or on Σ_c X[FIX0,c] the result is void ('FIX-slice key -> void; SUM key -> void'). At protocol.zig:1255-1263 the .key branch calls setb on the whole tensor without checking that the term's labels are plain, distinct variable labels over all of its bits. That covers SUM, FIX0/FIX1 and, by the same reasoning, repeated or diagonal labels. The finding is real but latent: no current builder bounds a core-op input only through a sliced key, and the statement is public and chosen by the verifier or builder, not by the cheating prover. It turns into a soundness bug only if third-party or arbitrary statements are trusted after validateStatement passes, so medium (not high) is the right rating.
fix: In the .key branch, call setb only when the term's labels over refBits(t) are exactly the pairwise-distinct plain variable labels: no SUM, no FIX0/FIX1, no repeats. The variable count must equal the tensor's bit count (for example, require the label mask to have popcount nb and every label below k.n). Otherwise do not record a bound, so the core-op check fails closed with StatementUnboundedOperand.

reason: I reproduced it with 'review: honest integer softmax is not normalised on flat rows'. The output is T=256 sum 2.000, T=512 sum 0.000, T=1024 sum 0.000. The arithmetic follows from transformer.zig:707-708: P has 1/128 resolution and each entry is rounded separately, so any key with weight below 1/256 rounds to 0. The reference test at transformer.zig:1223 only checks |psum−128| ≤ T, which places no constraint at T≥128. The bench layer configs use lt=9 and lt=10, so at those sizes the proved function is a badly distorted attention, while transformer.md §2 presents it as softmax. This is a semantics/fidelity defect, not a soundness one. Random-data rows are not perfectly flat, but rows with many comparable scores lose most of their mass in the same way.
fix: Use the same restructuring as EXT-1: compute the unnormalised acc=Σ_j e·v exactly and divide once per output with o=round(acc/den) via a division inequality. This keeps rows normalised to within one rounding per output and also removes the reciprocal. If P must stay, give it at least 2^16 units and requantise in PV. Tighten the reference test to |Σ_j P − 2^frac| ≤ a small constant and add a flat-row case at T=512.

reason: I verified each claim in the sources. README.md:5-7 says 'same statement class as FlashProve (... run on this prompt, produces these outputs)'. In fact buildStack (transformer.zig:932-940) takes x_in as a committed witness (bench.zig:343 uses model.randomInput), and there is no token binding, embedding, final norm, output head or argmax. FlashProve has these: docs/model.md:273-274 defines Model(tok)=argmax lam_(T-1). Bench weights come from randomWeights(-8,7) (transformer.zig:976). FlashProve clamps activations, queries and keys to ±2047 (model.md:46-47, 198-199) and range-checks weights up to 4095 (model.md:476). FlashProve's MoE has a router sigmoid scale and a shared expert (model.md:254-257); ours has neither, yet size.md:241-264 assumes a shared expert and sets ~0.42 MB against FlashProve's 18.78 MB. Partial mitigation: the README already states 'v1 is non-hiding' and that the zk numbers are reported separately (README.md:88-99), so the hiding part of the claim is disclosed. The statement-class and MoE/precision mismatches are not disclosed.
fix: Reword README.md:5-7 and size.md §5 to say the statement is narrower: committed I/O with no public tokens, int8 activations, weights in [-8,7] in the benches, top-1 MoE without the shared expert or router scale, the coarse softmax, and non-hiding. Report prove_s with forward time included, next to FlashProve's figure. Before claiming parity, implement the shared expert and sigmoid router scale, public-token embedding lookup, final norm, output head with a greedy-argmax gap check, 12-bit clamped activations, and bench weights over the full int range.

reason: I added the opt-in test ~/Coding/ge-wt/rev-ext/src/tensor/review_ext5_test.zig 'review: mleEvalI32 on a public value of 2^31-1 (accepted by xt.validate) panics', which runs only with REVIEW_PANIC=1. It is wired into the worktree's local mod.zig. The ReleaseSafe output is 'panic: reached unreachable code' at field.zig:190 in mleEvalI32. That function calls fromI32(2147483647), which reaches the m31.zig:28 assert. xt.validate (ext.zig:199-201) checks only the length of public values, not their range. Two related paths I found by inspection (not tested): fromI32(minInt(i32)) computes P+x = -1 and panics on the @intCast to u32, and termScale (ext.zig:488-492) panics or asserts once n_sum ≥ 31. The statement is verifier-chosen, so this is a robustness or DoS issue. In ReleaseFast it would silently produce a non-canonical M31 and wrong verification arithmetic.
fix: Implement fromI32 as fromI64(x), which reduces correctly for every i32 including maxInt and minInt. Alternatively, reject public and table values outside (−p, p) in xt.validate. In termScale, compute 2^n_sum with fromI64 or a field power, or reject terms with n_sum ≥ 31 in checkExpr.

reason: I reran src/tensor/review_parity_test.zig with `memguard run --gb 6 --label review-skeptic -- zig build test -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe --summary all` and got 'Build Summary: 3/3 steps succeeded; 59/59 tests passed'. The test 'MLP proof for input X2 verifies under the statement built from a different input X1' passes, and that pass is the defect: proto.verify accepts proof2 (input X2, a different output) against b1.statement(). protocol.zig:86-93 Statement has witness/weights/tables/ops plus ext.publics. ext.zig:82-89 can bind public tensors, but model.buildMlp (model.zig:58-60) and the layer builder never populate publics, so neither the input nor the output is bound. The proved relation is only 'there exist X, Y with Y = f_W(X)'. README.md:5-7 says 'targets the same statement class as FlashProve (the committed integer model, run on this prompt, produces these outputs)', which is false for the non-hiding path that every MLP/layer benchmark row uses.
fix: In buildMlp and the transformer Builder, register the input X (or the public prompt tokens and embedding) and the final output as ext.publics, so their MLE claims are checked by the verifier, as zk's mixPublic/publicClaims (zk.zig:1156-1175) already do. Add a test asserting that verify(statement(X1), proof(X2)) fails. Until then, label non-hiding MLP/layer rows 'no I/O binding' and drop the 'same statement class' wording.

reason: Reproduced: the test prints 'review-parity shifts X1={ 5, 5, 5, 5 } X2=X1/16 -> { 1, 1, 6, 4 }'. model.chooseShift (model.zig:23-32) derives each shift from the max |acc| of the current input's accumulators. The shift goes into Op.matmul/hadamard/glu.shift inside the prover-built Statement, and the verifier is simply handed built.statement() (bench.zig:176, :200). A client therefore cannot compute the statement from the commitment and the prompt. Fixing the shifts client-side does not help: requant is undefined out of range, so honest proofs would then fail on some inputs. Not demonstrated: the 'shift 29 collapses everything to a constant-output model' attack (I did not build that witness). It follows directly from the verifier accepting any shift ≤ 30 that passes the accumulator-bound check (protocol.zig:1278-1284), so the core claim stands.
fix: Introduce a public ModelConfig holding the per-op shifts (and the norm params and table ids), calibrated offline. Hash it into the weight key / commitment digest. The verifier reconstructs Statement from (ModelConfig, public input, claimed output) and never takes a prover-supplied Statement. Replace 'undefined outside int8' with a proved clamp: a range proof on the pre-clamp value plus a select, or FlashProve-style clamps.

reason: pcs.zig:43-49 provenBits = -t·log2(1-δ) + pow_bits is the query term only; pcs2.zig:78-80 takes the min of two such terms. The tensor_compare.py:41 comment '160 * 0.678 + 20 = 128.5 bits' is what drives the 'proven128' label. It leaves out the proximity/correlated-agreement error (~n/|F| ≈ 2^22/2^124 per proximity row), the LogUp terms, ~100 sumcheck/GKR rounds at d/|F|, and the QM31 ceiling (300/2^124 ≈ 2^-115.8). The codex/tensor-r2-sec security.md table (lines 232, 253, 326) gives 100.3 bits for the toy proven128 config with and without work, and 96.7 for MLP 512. Those numbers fit the 1-prox term at ~2^-100. So 'proven128' overstates the bound by about 28-31 bits and sits below FlashProve's 126.21-with-work whole bound.
fix: Rename provenBits to queryTermBits and the configs to 'ud-query160' / 'cap-query54'. Merge the r2-sec whole-bound calculator, and print the whole bound (with and without PoW) in every bench JSON row and in COMPARISON.md. To actually reach ≥ FlashProve, use ≥2 proximity rows (r2-sec: 114.3 / 106.9) and accept that QM31 caps the bound at ~114. Otherwise move the challenge draws to a degree-8 extension.

reason: In v2-merged/COMPARISON.md the toy table sits under 'Same statement, same machine', and its speedup column (15.4x-52.8x) sets our non-hiding proofs (results.jsonl has 0 zktoy rows, so the zk suite was never run for v2) against FlashProve's hiding deep runs at w0. RESULTS.md:155-156 shows that 51% of FlashProve's prover time is ChaCha20 for salts and mask tails and 30% is BLAKE2b. RESULTS.md:14 and :108 say EngineCpu is strictly sequential and SumcheckCpu is O(k·2^k) through std::function. RESULTS.md:246 says these are reference-code numbers, not CUDA. Security also differs (P3: ~100 or ~55 provable bits against FlashProve's 128-per-round target). One mitigation: the subtitle does disclose 'hiding on … Ours: non-hiding'. A partial refutation: PoW matching alone hardly moves the headline, because toy_L20_w20_deep.log gives 8.63 s / 12.5 ms / 307,864 B against w0's 8.37 s, so it stays ~52x. Hiding and security parity are the material confounders.
fix: Run the zk suite and make the headline toy row hiding-vs-hiding at matched PoW (FlashProve w20 rows). Add columns for whole-bound bits (with/without work) on both sides. Rename the section to 'Same relation (a∘b=c), same machine'. Label FlashProve numbers 'sequential CPU reference (blocks/, not cp_prove/CUDA)'. Move non-hiding rows to a secondary table with no speedup column.

reason: bench.zig:184 uses proveWithAccumulators with built.accs from the forward pass, and bench.zig:222 computes proved_macs_per_s = macs/prove_s. For mlp-proven128-t11: 2.0616e11/2.0552 = 1.00e11, whereas over prove+forward (3.037 s) it is 6.8e10. The data also shows the noise inversion: proven128-t11 prove 2.055 s < conj128-t11 2.257 s, and the same at layer t10 (5.546 vs 4.773). I lowered severity to low because the table header does show 'prove (+ integer forward)' with the forward time listed separately. Only the MAC/s and µs/token columns mislead, and n=1 noise is a hygiene problem, not a correctness one.
fix: Report proved_macs_per_s over (forward_s + prove_s), or add a second column for it. Make tensor_compare set TENSOR_PROVE_REPS≥3 with a warm-up and report median and range. Record load average and AC state per row. Flag rows where a costlier config came out faster.

reason: Reproduced at tiny size with the built tensor-bench. 'layer 4 5 6 1 1 54 2 20 0 1 2 54' prints 'error: BadConfig'. The correctly laid-out 'layer 4 5 6 1 1 54 2 20 0 1 0 4 1 2 54' succeeds (log_experts 0, log_capacity 4). tensor_compare.py:91 passes ['layer', lt, 11, 12, 4, 12, q, lb, pw, 2, 1] + ex, so ex[0..1] land in args[12..13] (bench.zig:313-314: le=2, lcap=54/160). transformer.zig:407 then rejects lcap > log_t. run_one turns the failure into {'error':…}, and report (tensor_compare.py:157) filters on 'prove_s', so the layer table silently disappears. The v2 layer rows have no log_experts field, which confirms they came from an older parser and cannot be reproduced at HEAD.
fix: In tensor_compare.py:91, insert 0, lt, 1 (log_experts, log_capacity, fused) before ex. Better, switch bench layer to key=value args. Make cmd_report exit nonzero when any planned tag is missing or has 'error'.

reason: weight_key.verify (weight_key.zig:119-124) checks only the integer sum of histogram entries (u32 each) == 2^n_vars, and nothing caps log_rows+log_cols below 31. With ≥ p keys, an out-of-range weight value repeated p times contributes p/(α-v) ≡ 0. The prover can then add p to an in-range bucket (m_v + p ≡ m_v mod p) to keep the integer total at 2^n_vars. That breaks the range proof, and the weight-key header itself says it needs 'sum m_v < p'. The same applies to per-request LogUp relations with D ≥ p. This needs ≥ 2^31 weights (8+ GB int8), so it is unreachable at benchmark sizes and on this host, and I did not demonstrate it. It is a real latent soundness gap for the Maverick-scale projections.
fix: In weight_key.verify and in each LogUp relation's verifier, reject when keys + table rows ≥ p (or ≥ 2^30 for margin): error.LogUpCountAboveP. Chunk larger relations into sub-relations with fresh α and separate sum checks. Mark the Maverick extrapolation out of scope until then.

reason: zk.md:157 states the commitment serves 'about C_w/(8·30) proofs: about 17 at C_w = 4096', and zk.md:423 describes a chain of links. FlashProve's paper.txt:725-726 gives 710,324 copies and 688,127 batches per copy. The budget is enforced: zk.zig:696 always calls enableBudget, and zk_pcs.zig:478 charges before release. So there is no current ZK leak in-process. The restart-reset concern is not exploitable today because masks are not persisted. The finding stands as a large parity/serving-design gap, not a present leak.
fix: Size weight slots for long serving (large ℓ, as FlashProve does) and link each re-randomized copy directly to a fixed T0 commitment instead of a linear chain. If masks are ever persisted, persist the budget counter atomically with them and refuse rollback. Extend the ZK treatment to the serving split with a fixed per-model MoE capacity.

reason: Confirmed: weights in the bench are randomWeights(-8, 7) (bench.zig:152); activations are int8; transformer.zig:407 caps log_experts at 6 (≤64 experts); there is no fidelity measurement against a float reference anywhere in src/tensor or the reports. Partly refuted: the claim that 'honest proving fails often on real data' does not hold as the code stands, because chooseShift adapts the shifts to every input so that requant stays in range. That avoidance is exactly P2's defect, and fixing P2 with fixed shifts would expose the failures. I did not inspect the r2-serve lm.zig claims (they are not on this branch).
fix: Use fixed calibrated shifts plus proved clamps (see P2). Widen the activation and residual streams to 12-16 bits via rangeWide keys. Commit the RMSNorm gains and the embedding table. Support E=128 plus a shared expert. Publish top-1 agreement against a bf16/float reference on a public checkpoint before claiming fidelity parity.

reason: README.md:5-7 claims 'same statement class as FlashProve' (false, see P1). Lines 26-27 still say attention is 'on the codex/tensor-attn stream'. The status section says the weight range proof is 'Not yet added', yet weight_key.zig implements it with verify at :119. It also says ZK is 'the codex/tensor-zk stream', but zk.zig/zk_pcs.zig are merged into this tree. These are documentation errors; the real problem is the overclaim, and that is P1.
fix: Rewrite the Statement, Comparability and Status sections: non-hiding path = existential relation without I/O binding; hiding path binds public I/O; weight range proof present (weight_key.zig); attn and zk merged; security reported as a whole bound.

reason: The COMPARISON.md primitives table shows our RS 2^20 at rate 1/2 against FlashProve's 2^16 and 2^22, and counts 4-byte M31 symbols against 8-byte Goldilocks symbols. Its sumcheck row compares 'all rounds, per entry' with '~5 ns first round', and its extension-mul row compares QM31 (124-bit) with cubic Goldilocks (192-bit). The table's own column headers name the fields and hashes, so this is disclosed but not normalized. It is a presentation issue only.
fix: Measure at matching sizes (2^16 and 2^22). Add bytes/s and field-bits/s columns. Compare first-round sumcheck with first-round sumcheck.

reason: A grep across src/tensor finds no proof serialization or parser; the only 'encode' is the RS encoder in pcs.zig:71. Proof sizes come from struct-field sums (pcs.zig:420-425, protocol.zig:378/445, zk.zig:879). The verifier only ever consumes trusted in-memory structs, so its handling of hostile length and count fields has never been exercised. Reported sizes are estimates, so the size comparison with FlashProve's file bytes is approximate.
fix: Define a canonical binary encoding with explicit length prefixes and caps. Report the measured encoded length. Add a standalone tensor-verify binary that parses an untrusted file with bounds checks, and fuzz it.

reason: Reproduced in ~/Coding/ge-wt/rev-kern. Under ReleaseFast, the test 'review-kern: sumcheck verifier rejects a false claim carried by a non-canonical round eval' fails with `FORGERY: sumcheck verified false claim {2143944187, 428718740, ...} (true {..., 428718742, ...}) via s0 limb 1 = 3246655821 (>= p)`. Under ReleaseSafe with REVIEW_KERN_SAFE_PANIC=1 the verifier aborts with `panic: integer overflow` at sumcheck.zig:456 in verify. The mechanism is as described. sumcheck.verify (sumcheck.zig:442-456) computes cur.sub(rp.evals[0]) with no range check. M31.sub (m31.zig:71) computes (a+p)-b, which wraps by 2^32 ≡ 2 mod p when b >= p. Transcript.mixFelts hashes the raw limbs. The forgery could not be refuted. I lowered the severity from high to medium for one reason: the tree has no Proof decoder or serializer (grep finds none; proof_digest.zig only hashes), so today the hole is reachable only by a caller that builds a Proof struct from untrusted data. The bug is latent at the API level. It becomes critical the moment any wire format exists. Round evals are not Merkle-bound, so no other check catches the bad limbs.
fix: Make canonicity a verifier precondition and enforce it at entry. At the top of protocol.verify and zk.verify, walk every transmitted QM31 and return error.NonCanonical if any limb is >= P. That covers sumcheck round evals, finals, lookup_in_values, weight_values, PCS opening rows, and GKR masks and claims. Give sumcheck.verify the same check on rp.evals[0..deg], since it is also called directly. Any future decoder must build values with a checked constructor (fromLimbsChecked).

reason: Reproduced. `zig build test-metal -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe` gives `metal matmul mismatch at 0: cpu -7684 gpu -6916 ... expected 0, found 2746` in 'review-kern metal: matmul with activation +128 (max |x| == 128, fp32 path) matches CPU'. The cause is gpu.zig:490, `simd = max_abs <= 128`, together with kernels.metal:524 `out[i] = char(x[i])`, which maps +128 to -128. Two things limit reachability. The current builders cannot trigger it: weight-matmul inputs come from int8 ranges [-128,127], and transformer.zig:284 uses CPU proto.matmulAcc. The P in [0,128] tensor feeds an ext einsum, not accel. However, validateStatement admits a matmul input bounded by a range key that includes 128. model.zig:45 (witness build) and protocol.zig:702 (prover) both route through accel.matmulAcc. Such a statement on --metal therefore gets a wrong witness or accumulators, which is a completeness failure, and it breaks the 'bit-identical' claim in metal.md.
fix: In gpu.zig:490 use `simd = max_abs <= 127 and !g.matmul_int_only` (|x| <= 127 also covers -128 safely, but keeping it strict is simplest). Alternatively test min >= -128 and max <= 127 explicitly. Update the comments in metal.md and kernels.metal to read [-128,127], and add +128 to the metal matmul test.

reason: Reproduced in a regime that validateStatement admits, with honest coefficients. I added src/tensor/review_kern_skeptic_test.zig, 'review-kern-skeptic: colCombine(i32, 8) with |x| < 2^20, T = 2^13, honest eq coeffs', wired in via mod.zig. Setup: x = 2^20-1 everywhere, which a 20-bit range key (MAX_TABLE_BITS = 20) admits; lk = 1, so 20+7+1 = 28 <= 30 passes protocol.zig:1278; T = 8192; the coefficients are a real eqTablePar table. Under ReleaseFast it fails: `colCombine(bound 8) overflow in admitted regime: got {1048575, 2147483643, 2147483643, 2147483643} want {1048575, 0, 0, 0}`. The same call with bound 20 is exact. Cause: with bound 8, pcs.zig:345 sets chunk_rows = 2^23, so 2^13 rows × lv < 2^31 × 2^20 exceeds 2^63 before any reduction. Under ReleaseSafe this is an i64 overflow panic in the prover. The hard-coded 8 appears at protocol.zig:1024, protocol.zig:1687 and zk.zig:1455. A second issue is unproven: for EXT_EXACT_BOUND operands the accumulator check is skipped, so proto.matmulAcc's i32 tmp (protocol.zig:733) can also overflow. I found no shipped builder that sends wide or exact operands into a weight matmul, so the current benchmarks are unaffected.
fix: Compute bound[] once, from the same logic validateStatement uses, and pass it to the prover. At the three call sites pass bound[m.x] (use 30 for EXT_EXACT_BOUND) instead of the literal 8; the cheapest safe alternative is a constant 30 for i32. Also make proto.matmulAcc accumulate in i64, or have validateStatement reject EXT_EXACT_BOUND matmul and hadamard operands unless a real bound is supplied.

reason: Reproduced in both ReleaseSafe and ReleaseFast: 'review-kern: QM31.mul agrees with the mod-p reference on non-canonical limbs (base shortcut)' gives `got {2147483599, 15, 0, 27} want {2147483605, 15, 6, 27}`. The lazy path stays exact on extreme limbs (test 1c passes). Canonical inputs are unaffected, so this matters only through KERN-1, which feeds non-canonical values in. It is not an independent vulnerability.
fix: No separate fix is needed once the KERN-1 canonical precheck is in place. Document that QM31.mul, mulM31 and sub require canonical limbs (< P), and optionally add std.debug.assert on the base shortcut in safe builds.

reason: Confirmed by inspection. The arithmetic is unambiguous, and a test would abort the binary in safe builds. In kernels.metal:22, x = INT_MIN gives x + 0x7fffffff = -1, so uint(-1) = 0xffffffff, a non-canonical value ≡ 1 mod p, whereas the correct value is -2^31 ≡ p-1. In field.zig:29, @as(i64, P) + INT_MIN = -1, and @intCast to u32 panics in safe builds or is UB in ReleaseFast. Honest builders never produce -2^31 (every bounded tensor is far below that), so neither the prover nor the verifier can reach it today.
fix: Map via 64-bit modular reduction on both CPU and GPU. CPU: fromI32(x) = fromI64(x), or add an explicit P to x computed in i64 and @mod by P. Metal: `long r = long(x) % long(P); if (r < 0) r += P; return uint(r);`. Alternatively, reject INT_MIN at witness commit time.
